why_go: January is peak archipelago season. Temperatures hover 22–29°C, skies are dry, and ferry services to neighbouring islands are reliable. The Cellular Jail light-and-sound show runs nightly.

things_to_do: Snorkel at Jolly Buoy Island or Red Skin Island
Trek through Chidiyatappu saltwater crocodile sanctuary
why_go: February is the driest month with near-perfect diving visibility (28–30m). Ferry timetables hold firm. Tourist loads ease mid-month as holiday surges subside.
pack_list: Reef shoes for rocky beach entry

who_should_go: Photographers wanting clear water and light
things_to_do: Island-hop ferry circuits to Havelock and Neil Island
Visit Samudrika Marine Museum for marine life context
why_go: March is the last reliably clean month before pre-monsoon humidity climbs. Ferries run on time, hotel rates drop 20 percent off January peaks, and daytime temperatures stay comfortable at 25–32°C.

things_to_do: Dive the pristine North Bay coral gardens
Beach relax at Vijaynagar Beach, Havelock Island
why_go: April remains pre-monsoon with ferries operating normally. Humidity climbs to uncomfortable levels (80%+), but water sports continue at regular schedule. Hotel rates are off-peak.
why_not: Midday heat becomes oppressive (27–33°C), limiting beach time after 11am. Humidity exhausts many travellers.

things_to_do: Dive in first half before squalls arrive
Cellular Jail visit inside air-conditioned interior
why_go: The first half of May stays dry and ferry services remain reliable. This is the true low-season window with minimal crowds and rock-bottom hotel rates.
why_not: Pre-monsoon humidity exceeds 85 percent from mid-month onward. Late May often sees first squalls, which can suspend ferries without notice. Heat peaks 27–33°C.
Southwest monsoon hits full force. Rainfall totals 400–500mm, seas turn rough, and ferry networks collapse. Water sports shut down. Accommodation floods in low-lying areas.
Peak monsoon. Rainfall 450–500mm. The entire ferry network shuts down. Do not book an Andaman trip in July under any circumstances.
Monsoon continues unabated. Rainfall 400–450mm. Ferries remain unreliable. Dive operators are closed. Skip entirely.

things_to_do: Cautious island exploration if ferries run
Cellular Jail visits during clear windows
why_go: Recovery month. Rainfall eases to 250–300mm and ferries begin returning mid-month, though cancellations remain likely.
why_not: Ferry services remain unpredictable due to lingering monsoon swells. Expect frequent cancellations and last-minute changes.

things_to_do: Ferry circuits recommence to outer islands
Snorkelling at Jolly Buoy as waters clear
Beach walks as rain decreases late month
why_go: Season officially opens. Rainfall 100–150mm, mostly in the first week, and ferries fully restore by mid-month. Temperatures settle to 24–31°C.
why_not: Monsoon winds still cause unpredictable ferry delays to nearby islands early in the month.

things_to_do: Diwali light displays across the islands
why_go: Peak season builds. Rainfall drops to 50–80mm. NE monsoon residue calms by November, and ferries run reliably. Diwali week draws celebration crowds.

things_to_do: New Year's Eve celebrations at Port Blair resorts
why_go: Peak season. Temperatures 23–29°C, skies dry, dive visibility 28–30m. Christmas–New Year rates spike 50 percent and ferries sell out.
pack_list: Formal wear for New Year's events

things_to_do: Sunrise walk along Rock Beach Promenade
Explore White Town's French Quarter colonial streets
why_go: Peak Coromandel window. Temperatures 21–30°C. The NE monsoon has spent itself. Aurobindo Ashram's Samadhi sees its quietest month, allowing contemplative space.
pack_list: Comfortable walking shoes for old-town streets
Sarong or shawl for ashram entrance

things_to_do: Mother's Birthday darshan (Feb 21) at Sri Aurobindo Ashram
why_go: February is the driest stretch with temperatures 22–31°C. Mother's Birthday (21 Feb) draws significant but contemplative crowds. Heritage Festival mid-month features cultural performances.

things_to_do: Explore Goubert Avenue and restored colonial buildings
Evening French Quarter cafes and boutiques
Serenity Beach for quiet sunset walks
why_go: Last cool window before pre-summer heat. Temperatures 24–33°C. Hotel rates drop 20 percent. French Quarter walks shift to morning and evening hours.
Pre-summer heat arrives (26–36°C), but April 24 darshan at the ashram draws pilgrims. French Quarter walks compress to 7–9am. Hotel rates drop further.
why_not: Midday heat exceeds 35°C, confining all outdoor time to early mornings and evenings.

why_go: Off-peak rates hit their lowest. Promenade evening strolls are the only viable outdoor activity.
why_not: Peak heat 27–38°C and humidity 85 percent make daytime exploration unbearable. Pre-monsoon thunderstorms arrive late month.

why_go: Pre-NE monsoon humidity peaks while monsoon rains arrive, creating dramatic but wet conditions. Rainfall 80–100mm.
why_not: Pre-monsoon humidity peaks while monsoon rains haven't yet arrived to cool things down. Tourist comfort is at its lowest annual point.

things_to_do: Bastille Day (14 Jul) French Embassy parade and celebrations
why_go: Bastille Day (14 Jul) brings unique French-Indian cultural celebrations. The French Embassy organizes a distinctive parade. Temperatures 26–34°C with sporadic rain.
why_not: Northeast monsoon rains will drench beaches and limit outdoor activities beyond the festival itself.
pack_list: Formal wear for Bastille Day events

things_to_do: Ashram facilities for Aug 15 Independence Day celebrations
why_go: August 15 (Indian Independence Day) brings ashram-centred celebrations. Late-summer humidity abates slightly. Rainfall 80–100mm.
why_not: Monsoon rains peak in August, making beaches unusable and outdoor exploration difficult. Ashram facilities may close for Aug 15 events.

things_to_do: Recovery-month beach walks as rain eases
why_go: Recovery month. Rainfall 100–150mm. SW monsoon retreats. NE monsoon arrives mid-October. Temperatures 25–32°C begin moderating.
why_not: Northeast monsoon rains flood beaches and streets throughout September, limiting outdoor time.

things_to_do: Rock Beach promenade walks as NE monsoon stabilises
why_go: Season opens but NE monsoon remains active. Temperatures 24–30°C. Rainfall 200–300mm. Cyclone risk exists in the Bay of Bengal.
why_not: Lingering monsoon rains still limit beach days and outdoor exploration.

why_go: NE monsoon at peak (300–400mm rain, but structured). Temperatures 24–29°C. Nov 24 Mother's Nirvan Day brings major ashram observance. Cyclone risk fades by week three.
why_not: Occasional post-monsoon showers may interrupt beach time and outdoor exploration.

why_go: Peak Coromandel month. Temperatures 22–29°C. NE monsoon retreating. Christmas–New Year draws 50 percent premium, and French Quarter books out.

things_to_do: Pamban Bridge dramatic crossing and photos

things_to_do: Temple corridor walks compressing to mid-day

why_go: SW monsoon spillover eases heat to 27–34°C. Sea breeze returns. Temple continues full ritual tempo.

why_not: NE monsoon rains expose temple tanks and the Pamban causeway drive to heavy weather early month.

why_go: NE monsoon active (250–300mm structured rain, 24–30°C). Char Dham peak builds. Cyclone watch active but lessening.

Amkunj 1.2km mangrove boardwalk walk (longest in India)

things_to_do: Cuthbert Bay nesting at full intensity observation
